newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt mixed, awaits 30-year auction.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt mixed, awaits 30-year auction.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were narrowly mixed in quiet trade at late afternoon as players kept to the sidelines awaiting Thursday's 30-year U.S. Treasury auction, traders said.

"I think after tomorrow's 30-year auction we might get a bid to the market and maybe take it higher, but there is really nothing going on today," said one head trader at a major U.S. investment bank, who noted that most of the activity was dealer driven. "It was an extremely boring day."
Looking ahead, sources said the price of Russian loans is likely to appreciate as pricing of the Eurobond nears.
"I think there is a lot of upside for Russian bradies ahead of the new Eurobond issue. Bradies are sure to rally on that," said one market source.
The Russian Eurobond issue, which is expected to begin its roadshow on November 11, will be the first bond in more than 80 years that the government will issue overseas.
The size of the deal is still uncertain, but one source said talk is that it could be as much as $500 million.
Price talk on the issue is currently around 350 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.
Sources said news on Tuesday that Russian president Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery was a success also helped to renew investor confidence.

"The fact that Yelstin's operation was successful is a stamp of approval from doctors that he can be in power and that bascially rules out any demands of the opposition to impeach him on the basis of incapacity. So basically it is a signal that the current government is here to stay," the second source said.

At 1700 EST/2200 GMT, Russian dollar-demoninated Vneshekonombank loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were unchanged at 77-3/4 bid, while mark loans RUVNDMLNS=RR were 1/8 softer at 82-1/8 bid and Min Fin 3s RU3E99=RR were 3/8 better at 81-7/8.
Meanwhile, the reelection of U.S. President Bill CLinton to a second term had little impact on the market.

Among Latin Bradies, sources said prices were range-bound most of the day. Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR were 1/8 firmer at 83-1/2 bid, while Brazilian "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were 1/8 weaker at 71-1/8 bid and Mexican UMS-26 MXUMS=RR were 1/2 lower at 101-1/2. -- Diane Craft, 212-859-1674
